subject: Throughput fallback request: reserved nodes & queueing for BrightLeaf
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightleaf.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool throughput / queueing behavior — request

Hi Sergio,

We run a mixed workload (real-time chat + nightly batch scoring) and are considering a reserved GPU pool with Redwood Dedicated. We need clarity on two things before procurement will sign: 1) an SLA commitment for sustained throughput during our nightly windows (90–240s sustained windows where throughput must not drop below X tokens/sec) and 2) queueing behavior — what happens when transient spikes exceed our reserved throughput (does Redwood queue, throttle, or burst to shared capacity?).

Attached is our SLA request form with target throughput numbers and a small sample of traces. Can the dedicated offering include explicit fallback/priority rules so our inference jobs don’t sit behind other tenants? If not, procurement will need exception language in the contract.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync.

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform
BrightLeaf Analytics

Attachments: BrightLeaf_SLA_Request_Form.pdf (pdf), queue-traces-20260110.zip (zip - 12MB)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool throughput / queueing behavior — request

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask and the form. I received the traces. Quick replies up front: we can provide a dedicated pool with an SLA for availability and a baseline throughput promise for pinned capacity. Queueing behavior depends on how you want to prioritize: we can set a strict reserved band (no bursting) or allow controlled bursting to shared capacity with priority queuing for your pool.

Couple of next steps I suggest:
- Can you confirm the sustained tokens/sec floor you need (you mentioned rates in the form, but I want the hard number Redwood should guarantee)?
- Are you open to a burst policy (you pay overage) or do you require hard isolation (no bursting, but a higher committed capacity)?

I’m looping in Karthik for sizing and Evelyn for SRE constraints. Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to align?

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: preliminary sizing notes for BrightLeaf

Quick internal note — looked at the traces Oliver sent. Summary:
- Nightly scoring spikes run for ~4–5 minutes, peak token/sec ~3x baseline.
- Average concurrent sequences during peak: ~120 streams at 1.2k tokens/window.
- If BrightLeaf requires a hard floor of 150k tokens/sec sustained for 5 minutes, that maps to approximately 6 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs with our serving profile (quantized medium-latency config).

Trade-offs: hard isolation (no bursting) will require a higher reserved commit and is the simplest SLA to write. Allowing controlled burst with priority queuing reduces commit but requires documented fallback policies and overage billing.

I’ll draft a proposal doc after Evelyn confirms the operational constraints.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightleaf.ai>, BrightLeaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed options for reserved pool behavior (BrightLeaf)

Oliver — thanks for the quick reply. Based on internal sizing, here are two paths we can offer:

Option A — Hard-reserved (no bursting)
- Dedicated pool sized to meet your sustained floor (example: 6 reserved GPUs)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on the reserved pool and a guaranteed throughput floor of 150k tokens/sec for 5-minute windows during committed hours
- No sharing or preemption; queueing only within BrightLeaf jobs
- Pricing: higher base monthly commitment

Option B — Reserved + controlled burst
- Smaller reserved commit (example: 4 GPUs) with priority queuing to allow temporary burst to shared capacity
- SLA: 99.95% availability of reserved capacity; when bursting, Redwood will attempt to serve excess requests from a higher-cost burst pool; bursts subject to dynamic overage billing and best-effort latency SLOs
- Requires explicit fallback language in contract describing throttling order, billing, and observable signals we will emit

If procurement needs explicit contract exception language, we can draft the text. Which option do you prefer? If you pick B, please confirm acceptable overage rate tiers.

If helpful, I can attach a strawman SLA document and the fallback ordering we propose.

—Sergio

From: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightleaf.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed options for reserved pool behavior (BrightLeaf)

Thanks — Option B aligns better with our budget if the burst billing is predictable. For procurement to move forward we need:
1) Exact language for the fallback/priority ordering (we need to show legal that our jobs will be first in line within our tenancy during bursts)
2) Defined metrics (what telemetry Redwood will publish when bursting and an event hook for sustained throttling)
3) Example overage tiers (per-10k tokens rates at low/med/high burst levels)

I attached a narrower set of traces that isolate the 5-minute windows. Please confirm whether your team can publish a dedicated metric (brightleaf.reserved_pool_burst_active) and an alerting webhook when sustained throttling > 2 minutes.

Oliver

Attachments: queue-traces-20260110.zip (updated subset)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposed options for reserved pool behavior (BrightLeaf) — engineering review needed

Evelyn — forwarding BrightLeaf’s preference for Option B and their telemetry/webhook asks. Can SRE commit to emitting brightleaf.reserved_pool_burst_active (boolean) and a webhook for sustained throttling >2 minutes? Also need language for fallback ordering that can be included in the contract (preferably: 1) BrightLeaf reserved pool, 2) BrightLeaf burst queue to shared burst pool, 3) general shared capacity). If SRE can’t guarantee the webhook SLA we need to mark as "best-effort" and capture in contract.

Can you review and respond so I can send the draft to procurement?

—Sergio

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed options for reserved pool behavior (BrightLeaf) — engineering review needed

Sergio — can do, with caveats.
- We will emit a metric brightleaf.reserved_pool_burst_active scoped to the BrightLeaf tenant; it will flip true when burst-serving is active. Metric will be available in our events bus within ~30s of state change.
- Webhook for sustained throttling: we can provide a webhook that fires when throttling persists >120s, but delivery is best-effort within our eventing SLA (we can commit to retry semantics and an SLA for webhook delivery only as a premium add-on).
- Recommended contract language (draft): "During burst conditions, Redwood will prioritize requests from the BrightLeaf reserved pool to the BrightLeaf burst queue before routing to general shared capacity. BrightLeaf’s reserved pool requests will not be preempted by other tenants. Bursting to shared capacity is subject to dynamic overage billing as defined in Schedule X."

Operational note: if procurement wants delivery guarantees for webhook latency we should scope to a Managed Events add-on with higher retention and delivery SLAs.

If that works I’ll ask Platform to add the metric and webhook in the staging org so BrightLeaf can validate next week.

—Evelyn
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>, BrightLeaf Procurement <procurement@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:41:00 -0800
Subject: Final: SLA fallback language & next steps

Oliver — following internal review we can proceed with Option B plus the Managed Events add-on if you need webhook delivery guarantees. Key points:
- Fallback ordering (contract): 
  1) BrightLeaf reserved pool (no preemption)
  2) BrightLeaf burst queue served from Redwood burst capacity (priority over general shared)
  3) General shared capacity
- Metric: brightleaf.reserved_pool_burst_active (available in staging for validation)
- Webhook: fires on sustained throttling >120s; delivery is best-effort unless Managed Events add-on is purchased (we will include retry semantics in Schedule X)
- Overage tiers: low/med/high examples attached to the quote (Marissa — attaching the pricing spreadsheet).

Action items:
- BrightLeaf to confirm acceptance of fallback wording and whether you want Managed Events add-on for guaranteed webhook delivery
- Procurement to sign the DocuSign that I’ll send once we confirm overage tiers

Link to DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/sealed/ABC12345

Thanks — will stand by for sign-off and can fast-track staging validation.

—Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
